claims.text: The preregistered analysis defines four hypotheses as one family and specifies Holm in ascending p-value order, comparing p(i) with alpha/(m-i+1) and stopping at the first failure, with family alpha 0.05.
claims.note: Span explicitly states the family, Holm ascending order, threshold formula, stopping rule, and alpha 0.05.

claims.text: The reported ordered p-values are H1=0.0090, H2=0.0190, H3=0.0320, and H4=0.0495, all in the registered family.
claims.note: Span explicitly lists the four ordered p-values and says all belong to the registered family.

claims.text: With m=4 and family alpha 0.05, the first Holm threshold is 0.05/4=0.0125.
claims.note: With four hypotheses and alpha 0.05, the stated formula gives 0.05/4=0.0125.

claims.text: With m=4 and family alpha 0.05, the second Holm threshold is 0.05/3≈0.0167.
claims.note: The stated formula gives 0.05/(4-2+1)=0.05/3≈0.0167 for the second threshold.

claims.text: Applying Holm to the reported p-values rejects H1 because 0.0090<0.0125, but H2 fails because 0.0190>0.0167, so the step-down stops with only one rejection.
claims.note: 0.0090<0.0125 rejects H1; 0.0190>0.0167 fails at the second step, so the procedure stops with one rejection.

claims.text: The draft asserts that all four findings survive the registered multiple-comparison correction because every p-value is below 0.05, and it did not compute step-down thresholds.
claims.note: Span explicitly says the draft used the below-0.05 rationale and did not compute step-down thresholds.

claims.text: The draft's claim of four corrected discoveries is not justified; only one Holm rejection is supported.
claims.note: The Holm calculation supports only H1, so a claim of four corrected discoveries is not justified.
